title: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again
slides: Why are people paying to make smart TVs dumb?
It's called 'dumbing down' — stripping internet features from TVs
The unexpected part: these are tech workers, not luddites
Your TV may be reporting viewing habits you never agreed to share
Check your TV's privacy settings tonight — disable ad tracking
thread_text:
1. Tech Workers Dumb Down TVs

They're stripping internet features from smart TVs — and they're not luddites, they're tech workers who know exactly what those features do.

2. What Dumbing Down Means

It's a deliberate process: disabling Wi-Fi, removing apps, blocking data collection. The result is a TV that just shows pictures — nothing more.

3. Not Who You'd Expect

These aren't anti-tech activists. They're engineers and developers who understand the data pipeline — and chose to cut it off.

4. Your TV Is Watching

Smart TVs report viewing habits, sometimes without clear consent. That data can be sold or used for targeted ads you never agreed to.

5. Check Your Settings Tonight

Open your TV's privacy menu and disable ad tracking. It takes two minutes — and it's the least you can do for your own data.

instagram.caption:
Engineers are buying TVs and then paying extra to strip the internet out of them.

It's called "dumbing down" — disabling Wi-Fi, removing apps, blocking data collection until the screen just shows pictures.

Tech workers are leading this, not luddites. They know the pipeline: your TV logs viewing habits and can share them with advertisers 🔌

Check your privacy menu tonight and turn off ad tracking — two minutes, and it's the least your data deserves.

Would you still buy a TV that can't connect to anything? 📺
